title: DC-area forecast: Pleasant sunshine today, before heat and humidity ramp up
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Bright sunshine with highs in the low to mid-80s today. Humidity remains comfortable, with dew points around 60.

What’s next? Heat and humidity start to ramp up tomorrow, with heat indexes next week making it feel like we’re back in July. By Wednesday, it could feel close to 100 degrees. Skies stay mostly sunny and dry to start the workweek before storm chances return by midweek.

Today’s daily digit — 7/10: A solid late-summer day, with lower humidity, plenty of sunshine and no rain to worry about. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Saturday): A warm and sunny start to the weekend, with mostly sunny skies and highs in the low to mid-80s. Dew points around 60 will keep humidity comfortable and less sticky. Winds from the northeast stay light at around 10 mph. Confidence: Medium-High 😎 Nice Day!

Tonight: Overnight lows range through the 60s. Skies remain mostly clear, but some clouds develop toward Sunday morning as humidity begins to creep back up. Patchy fog is possible as well. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Sunday): Heat and humidity start to build, with highs in the mid- to upper 80s. Heat indexes could reach the low 90s as dew points climb into the upper 60s. Winds from the southeast stay light at around 10 mph. A spotty shower is possible during the afternoon, but most of the day looks dry. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow night: Muggy lows dip into the low to mid-70s under partly cloudy skies. Confidence: Medium-High

Our morning forecast email is back! It's included with every level of support — from Free to Sustainer — delivered 7 days a week. Sign up at: capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

The heat is on. Highs reach the low to mid-90s Monday before climbing into the mid-90s Tuesday and Wednesday. Heat indexes rise into the upper 90s Tuesday and could approach 100 Wednesday, making it feel like July again. Dew points start the week in the mid-60s before climbing toward 70 by Wednesday, adding to the hot and muggy feel.

Skies are partly sunny throughout this stretch. Monday is probably rain-free before the chance of an isolated shower enters the forecast Tuesday. Chances for late-day showers and storms increase somewhat Wednesday. Confidence: Medium

Thursday may bring the week's highest chance of showers and storms as a cold front comes through. That should help temperatures trend back down, with highs to start Labor Day weekend dropping into the low to mid-80s again.

DC weather history for August 29

Unseasonable chill in 1986 tied a record low for August, while in 1988 the remnants of Tropical Storm Chris brought soaking rains and gusty winds to the region.
